subject: biology
title: The brain
key_idea: The brain is the coordination centre for most of the body. Different regions have different jobs: the cerebral cortex handles thought, memory and language, the cerebellum balance and coordination, and the medulla heart rate and breathing. (Separate science)

sections.heading: Regions of the brain and their jobs

blocks.text: (Separate science) The brain is part of the central nervous system. This section covers the main regions and what each one controls.

items.meaning: The outer layer of the cerebrum, or cerebral hemispheres. It is the part used for conscious thought.
The region at the back of the brain that controls balance and coordinates movement.
The region joined to the spinal cord that controls unconscious activities.
A region that monitors and controls body temperature and water balance.
An endocrine gland in the brain that releases hormones.

diagram.alt: A self-test: tap each region of the brain to learn its job, then test yourself.
diagram.prompt: Tap a region of the brain to see what it controls.

parts.name: Cerebral cortex
parts.detail: Controls conscious thought, such as making decisions. It also deals with memory, language, learning and voluntary movement. It processes vision.

parts.name: Cerebellum
parts.detail: Controls balance and coordinates conscious movement.

parts.name: Medulla oblongata
parts.detail: Controls heart rate and breathing rate. These activities are unconscious and automatic.

parts.name: Hypothalamus
parts.detail: Monitors body temperature and water balance, and controls the pituitary gland.

parts.name: Pituitary gland
parts.detail: An endocrine gland. It releases hormones into the blood.

items: Cerebral cortex: thinking, decisions, memory, language, vision.

blocks.text: Damage to one region affects the job that region does. Exam questions often give a symptom and ask which region is involved.

rows: Loss of sight, if the back of the cerebral hemispheres (occipital lobe) is damaged
Heart rate and breathing rate affected

items: The brain processes information from the eyes in the cerebral hemispheres.
Voluntary movement is controlled by the cerebral cortex (the motor cortex).
The cerebellum coordinates that movement, so it is smooth and balanced.
Match the symptom to the region that does that job.
The cerebral cortex is for conscious thought. The medulla works without thought.
Damage to a region affects the jobs that region does.

worked_example.question: Name the part of the brain that is responsible for making a decision.
worked_example.tip: Cerebrum and cerebral hemisphere(s) are also allowed.

worked_example.question:
A rat brain has 2.0 × 10⁸ neurones and a frog brain has 1.6 × 10⁷ neurones.

Calculate the difference between the number of neurones in the brain of the rat and the brain of the frog. Give your answer in standard form.
answer_points: In standard form this is 1.84 × 10⁸ (1.8 × 10⁸ is accepted).
worked_example.tip: A correct answer with no working scores both marks. 18.4 × 10⁷ or 18 × 10⁷ scores 1 mark.

worked_example.question:
Gillespie syndrome is a rare genetic disorder. People with Gillespie syndrome have eyes with no iris and damage to their cerebellum.

Person D is very sensitive to bright light and has difficulty controlling their balance.

Explain why this is.
answer_points: They have their iris missing and damage to their cerebellum.
The iris controls the amount of light entering the eye (the pupil).
The cerebellum controls balance and coordination.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each point. Link each symptom to the structure that is damaged.
